text.p: Credit ratings agency Moody's Investor Service said it confirmed the existing ratings for Swedish mortgage bank Stadshypotek AB after the announcement it would merge with insurer Skandia AB.
Moody's said about $500 million of long-term debt was affected.
In confirming the ratings Moody's said it did not view this proposed transaction as materially affecting the credit fundamentals of Stadshypotek, Sweden's largest mortgage lender.

"Stadshypotek's ratings are based on its strong franchise in the Swedish housing-finance sector, where it has a market share of 30 percent, and on the institution's improving performance and capitalisation," the ratings agency said.

Moody's said the strength of the underlying mortgage business should not be affected by the merger, and long term benefits both in terms of additional revenue generation and cost efficiency should be achievable.
The merger would result in the Swedish government disposing of its 34 percent interest in Stadshypotek.
The following ratings were confirmed: Senior Unsecured MTN A2, Commercial Paper Prime-1.
